title: Telephony RRC Statistics
description:
New feature to have RRC Statistics.

Related issue is #20319.

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • d56a5695 - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • 2e7bc3aa - Telephony RRC Statistics
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223364418&start_sha=e9d7cd94d460d6affaad4d98b7a4bcb191242bad)
This change seems unrelated
this is an earlier minor mistake, I thought to fix it with this merge. I guess you could fix it separately?
Why would it be a mistake? Why do you need a dissector registered by name for the the MIB payload? We already have a dissector the the BCCH-BCH payload.
The way we have direct dissectors for SIB2-SIB25 (nr-rrc.sib2 ...), we should have then for mib too along the same logic (nr-rrc.mib). That was my thought.
I agree to remove this change and patch from the original merge since this an independent issue. However, I think there is no harm to add this and allow dissect with `nr-rrc.mib`.

There is a use to decode a SIB outside of a BCCH-DL-SCH because some other protocols use this. Have you found a use case where you would have to call the MIB PDU dissector without being encapsulated in a BCCH-BCH? Let's not add a useless dissector registration by name unless there is a real need for it.
Understood. Even if I have a use case, which could be my own minor use case, you have a valid point so I agree to completely ignore this change and remove from this merge.

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223647021&start_sha=abd967aa7082b4f4bcf8425a978d5c9aea261010#fa2f75f52293f0ebb49b8904cce3dd8904069450_204_204)
This is the MIB, not a BCCH-BCH message (the tap should be in dissect_nr_rrc_BCCH_BCH_Message()). Moreover what's the point of having this info in the tap as is it broadcast periodically?

MIB is under BCCH-BCH, right?

![mib](/uploads/e427ca9e7ed64dadf2ce8832ae578fc7/mib.png)
The MIB is not the same thing as the BCCH-BCH message.

If you want to count BCCH-BCH messages, then in the future you could have another MIB format (see the extension choice in the `BCCH-BCH-MessageType`). The MIB payload is not the same as the BCCH-CH one. Anyway I find it completely useless to add the MIB to the tap (like the BCCH-DL-SCH) because it is transmitted every 80ms by the gNB (and even more often with the repetitions).

Understand and this resonates with your other comments below. I do not consider future choices since we can't predict that at all. That could be added whenever changes are made, same way you keep updating the source code when a new 3GPP TS release is out.

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223647021&start_sha=abd967aa7082b4f4bcf8425a978d5c9aea261010#fa2f75f52293f0ebb49b8904cce3dd8904069450_777_774)
Done, updated.
Moreover what's the point of having this info in the tap as is it broadcast periodically?
To be honest, I do not understand this comment.
Why do you need to count the SIBs broadcast periodically in the tap? Is this of any use?
I do not understand the part "periodically". I was just trying to create a statistics of the pcap, to count the RRC messages per type.
A SIB is sent periodically in the cell. I do not see interest of counting the number of times a SIB is transmitted.

I get it now, from the gNB to the UE. Okay. Yes, sure, that is periodic. But in a pcap most likely we won't have thousands of packets. Well, I understand your logic now, why to calculate something which is sent by gNB all the time. I added all message types including all the SIBs without considering to ignore any. To be honest, I was sure if I missed any type, someone would have told me to add the missing ones.

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223647021&start_sha=abd967aa7082b4f4bcf8425a978d5c9aea261010#fa2f75f52293f0ebb49b8904cce3dd8904069450_790_783)
Done, updated.
The tap should be in BCCH-DL-SCH-Message (the same principle applies to all instances below)
How can I add TAP under the Message when I do not know which `choice`? The reason I added under `c1` because there I can identify easily what message is this.
ok got it, but as indicated previously I do not see the usefulness of tapping the SIBs to count the number of times they were broadcast
then what else option I have? I mean, it's fine if you have doubts, but how can we do better then?
See my other comments: storing in the tap messages like BCCH-BCH, BCCH-DL-SCH or MCCH seems completely useless to me as they are always transmitted periodically.
Understood. So you think we should only consider some of the message types to count and skip other which are sent periodically?
Yes, if we consider such menu to be useful (I do not as stated in my initial comment).

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223647021&start_sha=abd967aa7082b4f4bcf8425a978d5c9aea261010#fa2f75f52293f0ebb49b8904cce3dd8904069450_2830_2671)

Done, updated. Please let me know if there is anything else.
Beside the last part, to approve this merge or not.
So how do we proceed?
The IEI column is meaningless for a RRC message
It is basically the sequence number from ASN... but yes, it does not have much value, indeed....
You want me to remove IEI column, right?
Yes as there is no Information Element Identifier in those protocols

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18623/diffs?diff_id=1223647021&start_sha=abd967aa7082b4f4bcf8425a978d5c9aea261010#e7906146662f52b315d7c54cfa76c096ddbf984e_916_915)
Done, updated.
The naming RRC3G, RRC4G and RRC5G seesm weird as this is not what 3GPP is using. Moreover you have not implemented any tap for UTRA and EUTRA.
yes, naming was not the best, but this is easy to change.
You want me to change to RRC_UTRA, RRC_EUTRA and RRC_NR right?
That would be better IMHO
Done, updated.

Hi,

here is a first partial feedback. Moreover you have not added the generated packet-nr-rrc.h and packet-nr-rrc.c files.

But more important I personally find the Telephony menu being already cluttered with things not related to telephony, and adding new statistics does not seem the right thing to me. Other might think differently so I will not prevent this from being merged. That said collecting this kind of stats for RRC does not seem useful to me as you are counting periodically broadcast messages and you are summing the RRC messages without any context of the UE for dedicated messages so I wonder what is the corresponding use case.

Hi Pascal,

I appreciate all the valuable feedback.

My original thought was to see a statistics of RRC messages because it can be useful during particular lab testing when there are few ten/hundred packets. Perhaps the TAP approach is not the right one?

Yes, indeed, I did not know I had to regenerate the .c and .h file, which I figured out in the meantime. Just don't know how to update this Merge request to add those...

Yes, for now I only considered NR, no UTRA or EUTRA yet. It was quite a bit of time to make these changes and I thought I would share NR only first, see feedback, before adding UTRA and EUTRA.

Naming convention, I agree with you, UTRA and EUTRA are better than my 3G/4G/5G.

This was just an idea, not necessarily a good one.

Was this tested on Windows? I recall that array exports using WS_DLL_PUBLIC do not work on Windows but I do not have a Windows machine to verify this.
I use Windows 11, I have not tried on any other OS. There are another 9 plugins which have WS_DLL_PUBLIC in .h file (under asn1).

So that is also wrong then?
As far as I can tell, all is done in packet-nr-rrc.c so why are you exporting those definitions in a header file?
Having something wrong in packet-tcap.c does not mean we should copy the same error.

There are 5 other plugins (under asn1 folder) which has `ws_symbol_export.h` and `WS_DLL_PUBLIC const value_string` used:
- ansi_map
- camel
- gsm_map
- h248

For example, `asn1\ansi_map\packet-ansi_map-template.h` has

If I searched correctly (under `epan\dissectors`), `ansi_map_opr_code_strings` is only used in `packet-ansi_map.c`.

I understand your valid point but then there are multiple other files with the same mistake in the approved code.
I was copying the logic, yes. But I was not aware this is actually wrong coding.
Those exports might have been necessary for a proprietary plugin, I cannot tell. But here this is definitely not the case so keep everything private in packet-nr-rrc.c.

IMHO it's quite unfortunate to have separate statistics for the c1 and c2 UL-DCCH messages (same applies for other messages, including UL-CCCH). Those are all UL-DCCH messages and there is simply an extension because the initial placeholder in ASN.1 was not sufficient. The split between is a technical detail the user probably does not care about (do you see any use for this?). Sorry for not noticing it earlier.

Because those are separated in the ASN1 structure (c1/c2), I have followed that at it was straight forward to implement. But then based on you comment, I will need to combine which takes some effort. For example, the value_string sequence won't match the sequence within ASN1 c1/c2 anymore which I used for easier matching.
Using the data_p->choice value to select the right value_string array as you suggest seems a good idea
yes, but it's the 2 arrays become one and the sequence numbers change for c2 items. So how do I refer to the c2 items? Use the + "c1 size" (e.g. +8) like that above?
Why do you want to combine the two arrays in one if you can select the right one based on the choice value?

Both tables follow the related value_sting array. This means one table for each array. 

So you agree to keep the 2 value_strings array but combine into one statistics table, right?
yes that's the idea
okay, I need to check how I can combine the 2 value_strings array into one `stat_tap_table_ui`.

I have often worked with RRC (3G, LTE, NR) in the past, though don't currently.  It never occurred to me to generate stats for RRC by message type.  What I've sometimes done (using internal messages from the product I was working on, rather than the RRC messages themselves) is to maintain a table of UEs (identified by some UEId) and their state.  So if you had one UE that hadn't answered an RRCReconfigurationRequest you could see immediately which one it is, rather than noticing that there are more requests than responses and then trying to work out which UE(s) was affected.
